title: Stream Decoding with Confidence Scores at Room and Cryogenic Temperatures
authors: Maries Tahaab, Tim Chan, James Kirkman, Simon C. Benjamin
abstract: In fault-tolerant quantum computing, fast and accurate decoding is crucial. Snowflake is a decoder for the surface code that runs in a streaming fashion. In this paper, we implement Snowflake on commercial FPGAs and validate them at room and cryogenic temperatures. Our results demonstrate high decoding throughput for small code distances that, when extrapolated, remains within acceptable limits for larger distances. Further, we incorporate the calculation of certain decoder confidence scores with negligible overhead both in terms of latency and physical resource utilisation. We note that implementing a large-scale system would require either a large FPGA beyond today's technology or clusters of FPGAs connected via a high-speed bus. Thus, we discuss an alternative architecture that exploits the locality of Snowflake by processing 2D slices of the 3D decoding window and offloading segments of the 3D structure to a high-speed memory.
summary: This paper presents a high-speed hardware implementation of the Snowflake decoder for quantum error correction codes, validating its performance at both room and cryogenic temperatures. The work successfully integrates confidence score calculation with minimal overhead, addressing key bottlenecks in fault-tolerant quantum computing. It also proposes architectural solutions to scale the system beyond current FPGA limitations.
main_problem: The core challenge is achieving fast and accurate decoding of quantum error syndromes, which is critical for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_result: The authors demonstrated high decoding throughput using FPGA implementation at both room and cryogenic temperatures while incorporating confidence score calculation with negligible overhead.
method: They implemented the streaming Snowflake decoder on commercial FPGAs, validating its performance across different temperature regimes and discussing architectural optimizations for large-scale deployment.
model_or_system: The system models Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (QECCs), specifically focusing on the surface code. The decoding process involves a round-wise streaming algorithm that processes syndrome information via a 'drop-grow-merge' cycle.
key_observables: Decoding throughput, reaction time, decoder confidence scores (DCS), and resource utilization (LUTs, FFs) are key observables.
important_parameters: Code distance ($d$), operating temperatures (room vs. cryogenic), and the required inverse throughput ($\le 1 \mu s$).
main_assumptions: The primary limitations discussed involve scaling to large code distances, necessitating alternative architectures that process 2D slices of the 3D decoding window.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of the Snowflake decoder for surface codes, contrasting full graph structures with proposed 2D distributed hardware implementations. Other figures detail the cryogenic measurement setup and state transition diagrams for the decoding cycle.
paper_structure: The paper details the necessity of fast decoding, presents the streaming Snowflake algorithm (using drop-grow-merge cycles), validates its implementation on FPGAs at different temperatures, discusses resource scaling limitations, and proposes an alternative 2D slicing architecture.
why_interesting: While focused on hardware implementation, the rigorous analysis of state propagation, cluster tracking, and error detection mechanisms within the decoding graph provides insights into complex dynamic systems that resonate with many-body physics modeling.
